title: Evidence fanout, reconciliation, and contract-versioning for compliance webhooks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a resilient fanout and reconciliation subsystem for audit/retention/residency events delivered via webhooks and the new Compliance Delivery API. This ticket covers the webhook contract versioning, delivery semantics (idempotency/retries), signed payloads, and a periodic reconciliation job that ensures downstream subscribers and our evidence ledger are consistent.

Goals:
- Define a minimal, extensible webhook payload and a contract-version header to allow safe schema upgrades without breaking customers.
- Implement fanout with per-subscriber delivery queues and exponential retry/backoff.
- Provide signed, region-aware evidence payloads with residency metadata and TTL markers.
- Add reconciliation that compares delivery ledger vs. subscriber acks and surfaces gaps to SRE/Compliance dashboard.

Success metrics:
- 99.95% on-time delivery to subscribers in same-region endpoints for P0 customers.
- Reconciliation detects and clears >95% of discrepancies within 24 hours.
- No breaking contract changes for v1 -> v2 migrations (all clients see X-Compliance-Contract header).

Non-goals:
- Full multi-region archival pipeline (separate project).
- Offline manual evidence export flow (handled by separate export job).

Design overview:
1) Contract versioning: Add HTTP header X-Compliance-Contract: v1 and X-Compliance-Contract-Signature for signed manifests. Webhook consumers must echo supported versions via a registration endpoint (console or API).
2) Payload: Each event will include a stable delivery_id, event_type, timestamp_utc, residency_hint, retention_ttl_seconds, evidence_bucket_url (signed), and an integrity signature. Example payload (stringified below).
3) Delivery semantics: Fanout service writes canonical event to evidence-ledger (immutable), enqueues delivery to subscriber queues (per-customer, per-region). Each delivery includes an idempotency key equal to delivery_id. A successful HTTP 200 (consumer) or 202 (accepted) marks delivery success; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff and dead-letter to Compliance Ops after N attempts.
4) Signing & verification: Use KMS-backed signing key per-region. Header X-Compliance-Signature: sig_v1=..., key-id:region-1. Consumers may verify using public key endpoints.
5) Reconciliation: Nightly reconciliation job compares evidence-ledger state -> delivery ledger -> subscriber ack logs. Discrepancies generate a grouped alert and a dashboard row with root-cause suggestions (network outage, invalid sig, consumer 4xx).
6) Backfill & replay: Provide a /replay API to re-enqueue specific delivery_ids for a subscriber with filters (date range, event_type). Replays are rate-limited and require audit logging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema documented in Confluence with examples and a migration guide.
- Contract header X-Compliance-Contract is present and respected by runtime; schema version returned in subscription metadata.
- Delivery ledger persists each attempt and final state (delivered, failed, dead-letter) with timestamps.
- Signed payloads are verifiable via public key endpoint and signature failures are logged and not retried for more than 3 attempts.
- Reconciliation job exposes discrepancies in the Console as a table with drilldown to delivery attempt traces.
- End-to-end integration test that simulates consumer returning 500 then 200 and shows retries + final delivered state.

Lightweight API / Webhook payload sample (single-line JSON string for docs):
{"delivery_id":"d_20250212_0001","event_type":"evidence.created","timestamp_utc":"2025-02-12T18:32:12Z","residency_hint":"eu-west-1","retention_ttl_seconds":"31536000","evidence_bucket_url":"https://storage.redwood.example/s3/evidence/d_20250212_0001?sig=...","metadata":"{\"model\":\"redwood-rl-1\",\"request_id\":\"r_abc123\"}"}

Operational considerations:
- Rate limiting: Per-subscriber burst and sustained limits with token bucket to avoid thundering herd.
- Cost: Fanout will increase egress; provide a dedicated tier and allow customers to choose polling vs. push.
- Observability: Trace ids should propagate via header X-Compliance-Trace. Add per-delivery cost estimate to Console.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Evidence+Fanout+and+Contract+Versioning
- API spec (proto & OpenAPI): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/compliance/delivery-api/openapi.yaml
- Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876
- Spike notes and load numbers: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-spike

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize schema & headers, CI contract tests, and public-key endpoints.
- Week 2: Implement fanout queue + delivery ledger and simple retry behavior. Add unit tests.
- Week 3: Reconciliation job, Console surface + alerts, integrate KMS signing.
- Week 4: End-to-end test, run on staging, and gradual rollout behind feature flag for P0 customers.

Rollout & migration notes:
- Feature gated behind account-level flag. New subscriptions default to v1. When v2 introduced, runtime will send both X-Compliance-Contract and an envelope header to allow old consumers to ignore v2-only fields.

Notes on privacy/residency: Always include residency_hint and region-coded signed evidence_url. For customers that require region-anchored delivery, we will only deliver from endpoints in matching region and mark event as region_locked in ledger.
